question: For every positive real number $x$, let $g(x)=\lim _{r \rightarrow 0}((x+1)^{r+1}-x^{r+1})^{1/r}$. What is the limit of $g(x)/x$ as $x$ goes to infinity?

\begin{align*}
g(x) &= \lim_{r \rightarrow 0} \left( (x+1)^{r+1} - x^{r+1} \right)^{1/r} \\
&= \lim_{r \rightarrow 0} \left( (x+1)^r - x^r \right) \\
&= \lim_{r \rightarrow 0} \left( (x+1)^r - x^r \right) \cdot \frac{x^{-r}}{x^{-r}} \\
&= \lim_{r \rightarrow 0} \left( \left( \frac{x+1}{x} \right)^r - 1 \right) \\
&= \lim_{r \rightarrow 0} \left( e^{r \ln \left( \frac{x+1}{x} \right)} - 1 \right) \\
&= \lim_{r \rightarrow 0} \left( e^{r \ln \left( 1 + \frac{1}{x} \right)} - 1 \right) \\
&= \lim_{r \rightarrow 0} \left( 1 + r \ln \left( 1 + \frac{1}{x} \right) + O(r^2) - 1 \right) \\
&= \lim_{r \rightarrow 0} r \ln \left( 1 + \frac{1}{x} \right) \\
&= \ln \left( 1 + \frac{1}{x} \right) \\
\end{align*}
Now, we have
\begin{align*}
\lim_{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{g(x)}{x} &= \lim_{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\ln \left( 1 + \frac{1}{x} \right)}{x} \\
&= 0
\end{align*}
The answer is (E).
